explanation: In an EC2 Image Builder pipeline that creates images on a schedule, the build components of the recipe apply the patches and the agent, the image is distributed only when all test components succeed, and the distribution configuration specifies the Regions and account sharing. A self-built cron script requires you to operate the server and script yourself and to implement guarantees such as distributing only after tests pass. An AWS Backup recovery point is a feature for copying backups and has no patch application or testing stages. Entering the ImageId manually does not solve the problem of creating the AMI and leaves only manual work.

prompt: Under security policy, the operations team of a public agency system must let administrators connect with a shell to 50 EC2 instances in private subnets that have no public IP addresses and no internet route. Inbound port 22 must not be opened, and bastion hosts and SSH keys must not be operated. Access permissions must be controlled with IAM, and connection records must be kept. The latest SSM Agent is installed on the instances. Administrators sign in with AWS IAM Identity Center, and the team wants to keep session logs in Amazon S3 or Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Which TWO actions are required to meet these requirements by using Session Manager? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new key pair for each instance, distribute it to the administrators, and operate a procedure to rotate the keys every 90 days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager (ssm, ssmmessages, ec2messages) so that the instances can connect to the service without the internet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach to the instance profile an IAM role that includes the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy so that the instances become Systems Manager managed nodes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Place a bastion host in a public subnet, allow only port 22 connections from the administrators' IP range in the security group, and connect again from the bastion to each instance by using SSH keys.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Assign public IP addresses to the instances, open port 22 for the administrators' IP addresses in the security group, and connect by using EC2 Instance Connect.

explanation: The correct answers are attaching a role that includes AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to the instance profile and creating interface VPC endpoints for Systems Manager. The former is needed so that the instances register as managed nodes and access can be controlled with IAM, and the latter lets the SSM Agent connect privately to the service from private subnets that have no internet route. Depending on the agent version, ec2messages is also used, so create all three endpoints together. A bastion host requires port 22 and host operations, which violates the constraints. Distributing and rotating key pairs works against the goal of eliminating SSH key management. Assigning public IP addresses and opening port 22 violates both the condition that there be no internet route and the condition that inbound ports not be opened.

prompt: A legacy application running on a single EC2 instance at an internal business systems company occasionally stops responding because of an OS kernel problem. When this happens, only the instance status check fails and the system status check passes. The instance must be rebooted without human intervention while keeping its public IP address, instance ID, and disk data, and a configuration that replaces the instance with a new one is not allowed. The application is already configured to start automatically after a reboot. An Elastic IP address is attached to the instance, a reboot finishes in about 1 minute, and the company wants the alarm to act only after 3 consecutive failed evaluations. What is the MOST suitable method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_Instance metric and specify rebooting the EC2 instance as the alarm action.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_System metric and specify recovering the EC2 instance as the alarm action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put the instance in an Auto Scaling group with minimum and maximum capacity of 1, and have the group replace it with a new instance when a health check fails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an EventBridge rule that runs an SSM Automation to stop and start the instance when CPUUtilization stays below 1% for 5 minutes.

explanation: The correct answer is attaching a reboot alarm action to the instance status check failure metric. The problem scenario is an OS-level problem in which only the instance status check fails, the metric that watches for that signal is StatusCheckFailed_Instance, and the reboot action keeps the instance ID and EBS data as they are. The system status check metric and the recover action are for host hardware problems, and the documentation also explains that automatic recovery does not work when only the instance status check fails. Auto Scaling replacement creates a new instance, which violates the condition to keep the instance. A low CPU signal often produces false positives unrelated to a kernel problem, and stop and start can change the host so that the public IP address may change.

prompt: The development account of a startup repeatedly exceeds its monthly budget of $5,000. The team wants to notify the owner when forecasted cost reaches 80% of the budget, and to automatically restrict the creation of new resources when it reaches 100%. There are 15 developers and no dedicated FinOps staff, so custom-built automation must be minimized. Notifications must be delivered both to the owner's email and to an SNS topic. The development account is a separate AWS Organizations member, the budget owner is comfortable with the Budgets console, and the restriction on creating resources must not block read operations. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Save a daily cost report in Cost Explorer, and have the owner check it every day and manually revoke IAM permissions if the budget is exceeded. When costs exceed the threshold, the owner directly checks and adjusts the resource creation permissions in the account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Receive Trusted Advisor cost optimization check results with EventBridge and have a custom-written Lambda function stop resources in the development account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a CloudWatch billing alarm to send a notification through SNS when the threshold is reached, and have the owner restrict permissions manually afterward.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set up an 80% forecasted cost alert through SNS on an AWS Budgets cost budget, and configure a budget action that applies an IAM policy denying resource creation at the 100% threshold.

explanation: AWS Budgets can send alerts on actual and forecasted cost through SNS or email, and a budget action can automatically apply an IAM policy that blocks resource creation when a threshold is reached, so it meets both requirements without custom development. Cost Explorer is a tool for analyzing and viewing costs and has no alert thresholds or automatic actions. Connecting Trusted Advisor to Lambda does not match a budget-versus-cost criterion and requires custom development. A CloudWatch billing alarm provides only notifications and does not automatically restrict permissions, so it does not meet the automatic restriction requirement.

prompt: The operations team at a food delivery app company receives the web tier CPUUtilization alarm and the ALB 5xx error alarm separately through SNS, so a brief alarm on just one of them often causes a night-time page. Over the past month, most of the early-morning pages were cases in which only one metric briefly crossed its threshold. The team wants to page the on-call engineer only when both alarms are in ALARM at the same time, while keeping the existing individual alarms themselves for dashboard display. The team cannot build new code or separate servers. The evaluation periods of both alarms are 5 minutes, and the individual alarm widgets on the dashboard must remain after switching to a composite alarm. Which method is MOST suitable while minimizing changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double the thresholds of both metrics so that exceeding only one of them does not trigger a notification, and keep using the existing SNS topic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a composite alarm and connect actions such as rebooting an instance or running an Auto Scaling policy directly as the composite alarm's alarm actions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive each alarm's state change event with two EventBridge rules, and have Step Functions determine whether they occurred at the same time before paging.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a composite alarm that references the two alarms with an AND condition, attach the on-call SNS notification only to the composite alarm, and remove the notification targets from the individual alarms.

explanation: The correct answer is to attach the on-call notification only to a composite alarm that combines the two alarms with AND. A composite alarm evaluates only the states of other alarms, so it can reduce alert noise while leaving the existing individual alarms as they are, and the documentation also describes composite alarms as a way to reduce alarm noise. Doubling the thresholds lowers the sensitivity for detecting a single-metric failure, which differs from the requirement. A composite alarm can perform SNS notifications and create OpsItems, but it cannot perform EC2 actions or Auto Scaling actions, so connecting those actions does not work. The EventBridge and Step Functions combination has many new components to build and operate, which does not fit the goal of minimizing changes.

prompt: An online bookstore company runs its web service on m5 instances in the Seoul Region, but next year it plans to move some of it to AWS Fargate and relocate some workloads to m6i and c6i in the Tokyo Region. The company wants to lower costs with a 1-year commitment, and the discount must continue to apply even with these changes. Current average monthly usage is relatively steady, and the finance team requires the freedom to change configurations even after committing. Usage fluctuates within 10% per month, and the company prefers to pay a fixed monthly amount with no upfront payment. Which purchasing option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase a 1-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the m5 family in the Seoul Region to secure the highest discount rate on current usage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the current m5 usage so that the needed capacity is always secured.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan so that the discount applies to EC2 even when the instance family and Region change, and also to Fargate usage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Convert all workloads to Spot Instances to use the lowest unit price with no commitment, and have them restart to prepare for interruptions.

explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply automatically to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, Region, or operating system, and also apply to Fargate and Lambda usage, so the discount is retained when you move from c5 to m5, change Regions, or migrate from EC2 to Fargate. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a specific instance family in a specific Region, so they do not apply when the Region or family changes or when you move to Fargate. A capacity reservation secures capacity but does not provide a price discount. Spot Instances can be interrupted, so they are not suitable for an entire web service, and they differ in nature from a commitment discount.

prompt: The operations team at a travel booking company runs Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL as a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Month-end report queries slow down the primary DB, so the team tried to send the report queries to the standby instance, but there is no way to connect to the standby. The service requires 24-hour write availability, and the failover configuration must be kept. It is acceptable for the reports to use data that is a few minutes old. The report queries are read-only SELECT statements, and write throughput must not decrease just because the read load increases. What is the MOST appropriate way to separate the report read load from the primary instance while keeping the write availability configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable the Multi-AZ configuration and separate the endpoint so that the existing standby instance is used as a standalone read instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Find the secondary endpoint address of the standby instance in the console and specify it as-is as the connection address of the reporting tool.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a read replica and have the reporting tool connect to the replica endpoint, leaving the Multi-AZ configuration as it is.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raise the DB instance class of the primary instance by two sizes so that report queries and service queries are processed together on the same instance.

explanation: The correct answer is to add a read replica and send the report queries to the replica endpoint. The standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment is a synchronous replica for failover, and the documentation explicitly states that it cannot serve read traffic, so separating reads requires a read replica or a Multi-AZ DB cluster. Disabling Multi-AZ would violate the availability requirement, and the standby would not become a read instance. The standby has no separate secondary endpoint that you can connect to. Increasing the instance class does not separate the load, and contention on the same instance continues.

prompt: A retail company purchased a 3-year Compute Savings Plan. Because it is reducing some workloads, it is worried that the committed amount may not be fully used, and it wants to be notified right away if the commitment goes underused and is wasted. The alert criterion is when daily utilization falls below 80%. A trend of declining usage is already visible a few months after the purchase. Notifications should go to the finance team's SNS topic, and the company does not want to build a separate analysis tool. The Savings Plan was purchased in the organization's management account, and the budget can be created in the same management account. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a daily Savings Plans coverage budget and configure it to send a notification when coverage is below 80%.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a monthly cost budget with the same value as the committed amount and configure it to send a notification when forecasted cost exceeds 100%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a daily Savings Plans utilization budget and configure it to send a notification when utilization is below 80%.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an hourly EC2 usage budget and configure it to send a notification when usage falls below the committed hours.

explanation: A utilization budget tracks how much of the purchased Savings Plans commitment is being used and notifies you when it falls below a threshold, so it fits detecting wasted commitment on a daily basis. A coverage budget tracks the percentage of eligible usage that is covered by Savings Plans, so it drops when usage grows and more of it is uncovered, and it cannot tell you about a situation in which commitment is left over. The forecast alert of a cost budget looks at cases where spending grows, which is the opposite direction from an underused commitment. A usage budget tracks service usage itself rather than whether the commitment is used, so it cannot directly reflect wasted commitment.

prompt: An application at a payment services company publishes the value 1 to a PaymentErrors custom metric only when a payment error occurs. The company created an alarm on this metric with a 5-minute period, 1 data point, and a threshold of greater than or equal to 1, but during normal times with no errors the alarm remains in the INSUFFICIENT_DATA state and appears gray on the operations dashboard. This has led to complaints that it is hard to tell whether the alarm is working correctly. It is hard to add code that makes the application publish the metric when there are no errors, and the only alarm action needed is an SNS email notification. What is the MOST appropriate setting so that the alarm shows OK during normal times and goes to ALARM only when errors come in?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to notBreaching so that periods in which the error metric is not published are treated as normal values within the threshold.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to breaching so that periods in which the metric does not arrive are also treated as threshold violations, so the alarm always shows a checked state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the alarm's missing data treatment to ignore so that the previous alarm state is maintained during periods with no data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lengthen the alarm evaluation period to as much as one day so that the alarm keeps showing OK if data arrives even once during the day.

explanation: The correct answer is to treat missing data as notBreaching. For a metric that is published only when an error occurs, the absence of data means everything is normal, and the documentation also recommends notBreaching for such metrics. Setting breaching would put the alarm in ALARM during normal times with no errors, which is the opposite of the requirement. ignore maintains the current state, so the initial INSUFFICIENT_DATA state would remain, and once the alarm goes to ALARM there would be no new data to move it out of ALARM. Lengthening the evaluation period still treats periods with no data at all as missing, so the state does not change and only the detection of errors is delayed.

prompt: A backup server in the on-premises data center of a manufacturing company connects to a VPC through an AWS Direct Connect connection and must upload backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region without going over the internet. The VPC already has an S3 gateway endpoint, but access from on premises does not work. Under security policy, backup traffic is not allowed to use a public internet path, and the network team does not want to change the Direct Connect connection itself. The backup data is about 2 TB per day, and on premises already uses a Direct Connect private virtual interface. What is the MOST appropriate change that satisfies the requirement of not using a public internet path?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint in the VPC and configure DNS so that S3 requests from on premises are sent to the endpoint's private IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the Direct Connect virtual interface to the route table associations of the gateway endpoint so that the on-premises path uses the endpoint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a NAT gateway in the VPC and route on-premises traffic through the NAT to the S3 public endpoint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a condition that allows the on-premises CIDR to the gateway endpoint policy so that the endpoint accepts requests from that range.

explanation: The correct answer is to create an S3 interface endpoint and have on premises access it through its private IP addresses. According to the documentation, gateway endpoints cannot be used by resources over VPN, VPC peering, a transit gateway, or Direct Connect, and in such scenarios you must use an interface endpoint, which has additional cost. A gateway endpoint is only a route table target, and there is no concept of attaching it to a virtual interface. Going through a NAT gateway would use the S3 public endpoint and the internet gateway path, which violates the requirement. An endpoint policy only defines the scope of permitted access and does not add reachable paths.

prompt: The operations team at a manufacturer wants to view application log files and memory and disk utilization from 40 on-premises Linux servers and 110 EC2 instances together in a single CloudWatch. The definition of what to collect must be changeable in bulk in one place, without being managed separately for each server. With as many as 150 servers, per-server manual configuration is unacceptable, and the operations team has 4 members. Assume that the on-premises servers are not covered by Systems Manager hybrid activation. The log files are under /var/log/app, memory and disk metrics are collected at 1-minute intervals, and configuration changes must be applied without redeploying servers. Which TWO actions meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach an IAM role with the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy to the EC2 instances as an instance profile, and configure credentials with the same permissions on the on-premises servers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances to collect memory and disk utilization, and install and operate the agent only on the on-premises servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable VPC flow logs and send them to a log group, which also collects the application log files and memory utilization inside the instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Install the unified CloudWatch agent on all servers, and place a configuration file that defines the log files and metrics to collect in SSM Parameter Store so that each server retrieves it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upload logs to Amazon S3 from each server with cron, run a Lambda function from S3 events to convert them into memory and disk metrics and publish them, and have an engineer check failures weekly. Also operate a separate reprocessing queue for conversion failures.

explanation: The correct answer is the combination of deploying the unified agent to all servers with the same configuration file and granting the agent permission to write to CloudWatch according to the server type. The unified agent collects logs and system-level metrics on both EC2 and on-premises servers, placing the configuration file in a single location in Parameter Store lets you change what is collected in bulk, and permissions come from an instance profile on EC2 and from credentials on premises. Detailed monitoring only shortens the collection interval and does not add memory or disk metrics. The S3 and Lambda conversion requires custom development and operation. Flow logs are network traffic metadata and have nothing to do with in-instance logs or memory.

prompt: A news media company serves the JS and CSS files of its static website through Amazon CloudFront with a default TTL of 24 hours. The company deploys 20 times a week, but even after deployments some users still see old files. The company must maintain the cache hit ratio and must also avoid the cost of invalidation requests and the problem of old files remaining in browser and corporate proxy caches. The origin is Amazon S3, and the team can modify the build pipeline itself. The HTML files have a short cache time configured, and the team uses a build tool that can rename only the JS and CSS files with hashed names. What is the MOST appropriate deployment approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an invalidation request for the /* path immediately after every deployment to clear the cache at all edge locations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the default TTL to 0 so that CloudFront checks the origin for changes to the file on every request.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new CloudFront distribution for each deployment and switch the Route 53 record to the new distribution to separate the caches.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Include a hash or version in the file name at build time and upload under the new name, and have the HTML reference the new file names.

explanation: The correct answer is to deploy with the version in the file name. The documentation recommends versioned file names over invalidation when you update files frequently, because versioned names give you control over which file users receive even when old files are cached in user browsers or corporate proxies, and they incur no invalidation charges. Invalidation only clears the CloudFront edge cache, so old files that remain in browser and proxy caches can continue to appear until they expire, and it incurs costs depending on the number of requests. Setting the TTL to 0 eliminates the cache hit ratio. Creating a new distribution for each deployment adds the burden of managing DNS switchover and warming a new cache.

prompt: A SaaS company has a recovery time objective (RTO) of around 5 minutes and a recovery point objective (RPO) of a few seconds for the case where its three-tier application in the Seoul Region suffers a Region failure. The company wants a structure in which scaled-down web and app servers are always running in the Tokyo Region so that they can handle requests immediately during a failure, and only capacity needs to be increased. The cost of always running full capacity is a burden, and management has limited the DR budget to a fraction of normal infrastructure costs. The database can already use cross-Region replication. The data replication lag between Seoul and Tokyo is normally within a few seconds, and the Auto Scaling group in Tokyo is already running with a minimum capacity of 2 instances. Which cost-effective strategy meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure a warm standby in which a scaled-down version of the whole environment is always running in Tokyo, data is replicated across Regions, and the Auto Scaling target capacity is increased during a failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure a pilot light in which only the data replica and AMIs are kept in Tokyo and the app servers are kept off, and the infrastructure is started and scaled out during a failure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure a multi-site active/active in which a full environment with the same capacity as Seoul is always running in Tokyo, both Regions handle traffic, and data is replicated in both directions. Also place health check based routing between the two Regions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure backup and restore in which Seoul backups are periodically copied to the Tokyo Region and, during a failure, the environment is created anew with CloudFormation and restored.

explanation: The correct answer is warm standby. According to the AWS whitepaper, in warm standby a scaled-down but fully functional environment is always running, so it can handle requests immediately at reduced capacity and then only needs to scale up, which provides a short RTO while reducing normal costs. In pilot light, the app servers are off, so startup and additional infrastructure deployment are required and requests cannot be handled immediately. Multi-site active/active always runs full capacity, which violates the cost constraint. Backup and restore creates and restores the environment from scratch, so it is hard to meet an RTO of 5 minutes and an RPO of a few seconds.

prompt: Under the financial regulations that apply to an insurance company, database backups must be retained for at least 7 years, and during that period no one, including the root user and security administrators, may delete a recovery point or shorten the retention period. Backups are already managed with AWS Backup, and the auditors require a control that can prove immutability. The company wants to use its existing AWS Backup vault without introducing a new backup tool. The vault is already encrypted, the recovery points exist only in the Seoul Region, and the security team keeps vault change history in AWS CloudTrail. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply a governance mode vault lock to the backup vault with a minimum retention period of 7 years, so that only authorized IAM users can remove the lock.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply a compliance mode vault lock to the backup vault with a minimum retention period of 7 years (about 2,557 days), so that the lock becomes immutable after the grace period ends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deny the delete recovery point action for all principals with a vault access policy, grant the permission to change the policy only to a small number of security team administrators, and audit the change history with CloudTrail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Copy the recovery points to an S3 Glacier vault and apply an S3 Glacier Vault Lock policy to prevent deletion for 7 years.

explanation: The correct answer is a compliance mode vault lock with a 7-year minimum retention period. In compliance mode, after the grace period (at least 3 days) passes, the lock becomes immutable, so no user, including root, and not even AWS can delete the lock or the recovery points, and the minimum retention period enforces the retention lifetime. In governance mode, a user with sufficient IAM permissions can remove the lock, which violates the requirement that no one, root included, can do so. A vault access policy can be changed by a principal that has permission to change policies, so it cannot prove immutability. S3 Glacier Vault Lock is a different feature from AWS Backup Vault Lock and applies only to Glacier vaults.

prompt: A company with group affiliates must deploy the same security baseline IAM role to 60 accounts in a single organizational unit (OU) in AWS Organizations, and the same role must also be created automatically in any account added to this OU in the future, without any additional work. The security team does not want to create execution roles for StackSets in every target account by hand, and trusted access for CloudFormation StackSets is enabled in the organization. The role to be deployed is a simple configuration with a few security baseline IAM policies attached, and it is enough for the role to be created within a few minutes after a new account is created. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a StackSet with self-managed permissions, and each time a new account is created, create an administration role and an execution role and then add stack instances. The same work must be repeated every time accounts are added.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate CloudFormation stack in each account, and when a new account is added, have an engineer manually create a stack from the same template.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a StackSet with service-managed permissions, specify the target OU, and turn on automatic deployment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Declare cross-account resources in a single stack template in the management account so that it creates the IAM roles in all 60 accounts at once.

explanation: Service-managed permissions create the required IAM roles on StackSets' behalf and integrate with Organizations, and they support automatic deployment, which automatically deploys stack instances to accounts newly added to an OU. This meets both the constraint of not creating execution roles by hand and the requirement that new accounts be covered automatically. Self-managed permissions require you to create roles in each target account yourself, and the work is repeated for every new account, so the operational burden is high. Creating a separate stack per account makes consistent deployment and updating difficult and increases manual work. A single stack can create resources only in the account and Region it belongs to, so declaring resources across multiple accounts is not possible.

prompt: A company attached an SCP to a workloads OU that denies ec2:RunInstances in Regions other than ap-northeast-2. Users with AdministratorAccess in member accounts cannot create instances in us-east-1. However, during an audit it was discovered that administrators working in the management account can still create instances in us-east-1. Some workloads are currently run directly in the management account, and the company wants to apply its Region restriction governance consistently across the entire organization. The schedule allows moving the workloads that run in the management account to member accounts, and the organization already has a trusted SCP structure in place. What should the company do to meet this requirement most appropriately?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Because the management account is not affected by SCPs, move the workloads to member accounts where SCPs apply, and use the management account only for managing the organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach the same SCP once more to the organization root that contains the management account so that the deny statement also applies to users and roles in the management account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grant the management account administrators a service-linked role so that those users are subject to the SCP restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify the management account ID in the Principal element of the SCP's Deny statement so that the deny also applies to users in the management account.

explanation: SCPs affect only member accounts in the organization and do not affect users and roles in the management account, so workloads that need the restriction should run in member accounts where SCPs apply, and the management account should be used only for managing the organization. Attaching an SCP to the root still leaves the management account excluded. Service-linked roles are among the things that are not affected by SCPs, and granting one to a user does not make that user subject to SCP restrictions. SCP syntax has no way to target the management account by using a Principal element that specifies a particular principal.

prompt: A financial services company wants to detect when any of the 40 accounts managed with AWS Organizations communicates with malicious IP addresses or makes anomalous API calls. The security team does not want to enable VPC flow logs and DNS query logs by itself or to build a collection pipeline. The security team is small, so it is also hard to operate separate collection servers, and new accounts must automatically become targets. No account has ever enabled threat detection, and the team wants to view the findings in one place. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on flow logs in all VPCs and collect them in a central S3 bucket, and then periodically compare them against a list of known malicious IP addresses with Amazon Athena queries.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty for the whole organization from a delegated administrator account, and configure it to be turned on automatically for newly created accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable Amazon Inspector for the whole organization to detect malicious IP communication and anomalous API calls that occur on EC2 instances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Collect security group and network setting changes with an AWS Config organization aggregator and evaluate them with custom rules.

explanation: When enabled, GuardDuty automatically analyzes CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs, and Route 53 Resolver DNS query logs as independent streams, so users do not need to configure flow logs or DNS logs separately. A delegated administrator account can manage the organization's accounts all at once. Collecting flow logs and comparing them with Athena requires you to build and operate the collection and analysis yourself. Inspector is a service that finds software vulnerabilities and network reachability, so its purpose differs from detecting malicious communication and anomalous API calls. Config only evaluates configuration changes and does not detect threat activity.

prompt: The web tier of an online shopping mall runs in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB. During a large sale event, when the request count triples, response latency grows even though CPU utilization stays around 40%. This is because each request waits a long time for an external payment API, so CPU is not the bottleneck. The company wants to automatically add and remove instances in proportion to the number of requests processed per instance. The warmup time after instance launch is already defined, and the minimum and maximum capacity are also set. Load testing has already confirmed that a single instance can handle about 800 requests. Which method is the simplest to configure and tune?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In a target tracking scaling policy, choose the ALBRequestCountPerTarget metric and specify the target number of requests per instance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify the total ALB RequestCount metric as the metric of a target tracking policy so that instances are added as requests increase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a target tracking policy with an average CPUUtilization target of 50% so that instances are added when CPU rises.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimate the event time windows and create scheduled scaling actions that raise the desired capacity at the same time every day, one for each expected request volume.

explanation: The correct answer is a target tracking policy that uses ALBRequestCountPerTarget as the metric. This metric is the average number of requests received per target, so the number of instances is determined in proportion to the load, and you only need to specify the target value because AWS manages the alarms. According to the documentation, the RequestCount of the entire load balancer does not change in value when the number of instances in the group changes, so it is not a metric that can be used for target tracking. If CPU is 40% while latency is long, as it is now, a CPU-based policy does not trigger scaling. Scheduled scaling requires guessing the time pattern, and wrong predictions lead to shortages or waste, so tuning continues.

prompt: A healthcare SaaS company wants to back up the EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and RDS instances tagged Backup=daily every day and retain the backups for 35 days, and also copy the same backups to another Region for disaster recovery. Newly tagged resources must be included automatically without extra work, and the company does not want to operate separate backup scripts for each service. The operations team wants to view the backup status on a single screen. Some RDS instances use encrypted snapshots, and a KMS key must be available for restores in the other Region. Which configuration has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Put a 35-day retention rule and a copy action to the destination Region in an AWS Backup plan, and specify the resource assignment with the tag condition Backup=daily.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a Lambda function for each service daily on an EventBridge schedule that creates EBS snapshots and RDS snapshots and copies them to another Region with the copy API.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automate only EBS snapshots with an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy, and set the RDS automated backup retention period to 35 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create the backup plan in only the Seoul Region, and set up S3 Cross-Region Replication to replicate the backup data to the other Region.

explanation: The correct answer is an AWS Backup plan with tag-based resource assignment and a cross-Region copy rule. AWS Backup manages EC2, EBS, and RDS in a single plan with a schedule and retention period and provides the ability to copy backups to another Region, and when you assign resources by a tag condition, newly tagged resources are included automatically. Lambda scripts violate the condition of not operating per-service code yourself. Data Lifecycle Manager focuses on EBS, and setting the RDS automated backup retention alone does not meet the requirements for cross-Region copy and unified management. S3 Cross-Region Replication replicates S3 objects, not AWS Backup recovery points.

prompt: An infrastructure engineer at a startup received a report that an EC2 instance in a newly created private subnet cannot reach the OS patch repository (on the internet). The public subnet in the same VPC already has a NAT gateway, and an internet gateway is attached. The route table of the private subnet has only the VPC local route, and the security group outbound rules allow all traffic. Under security policy, the instance must not be directly exposed to the internet. There is only one NAT gateway, in a single public subnet rather than one per Availability Zone, and the company is keeping this configuration for now for cost reasons. What is the MOST appropriate action to solve the problem without directly exposing the instance to the internet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway and assign a public IP address to the instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the NAT gateway into the private subnet so that address translation happens in the same subnet as the instance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a rule allowing all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 to the outbound rules of the instance's security group to open external connectivity.

explanation: The correct answer is to add a route to the private subnet's route table that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway. A NAT gateway goes out through the internet gateway from the public subnet, and a private subnet has no way to reach external addresses without a default route, so the missing route is the cause. Adding an internet gateway route and assigning a public IP address directly exposes the instance to the internet, which violates the condition. If you move the NAT gateway into the private subnet, there is no route to the internet gateway, so it does not work. Security group outbound rules do not solve the problem of a missing route.

prompt: A manufacturing company must resolve a private hosted zone in a VPC (app.internal.example) from on premises, which is connected through AWS Direct Connect, and must also resolve corp.example.local, which is managed by on-premises DNS servers, from EC2 instances in the VPC. The company does not want to operate its own DNS server instances on either side. The network team has 2 members, and redundancy is needed because a DNS failure affects the entire business. The connection between on premises and the VPC already works reliably over Direct Connect, and endpoint ENIs can be placed across two AZs. Which TWO actions have the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC, and have the on-premises DNS forward queries for app.internal.example to the endpoint IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install BIND on EC2 instances in the VPC to configure conditional forwarding in both directions, point the on-premises DNS to these instances, and place one instance in each AZ for redundancy. Also manage the synchronization settings between the two servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint in the VPC, and associate with the VPC a rule that forwards corp.example.local to the on-premises DNS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify only the on-premises DNS server addresses in the VPC's DHCP option set so that the DNS queries from all EC2 instances go to the on-premises servers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Copy the records of the private hosted zone into a public hosted zone and publish them, and have on premises resolve them through internet DNS.

explanation: The correct answer is the configuration that uses an inbound endpoint together with an outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule. Route 53 Resolver cannot be used directly from outside the VPC, so an inbound endpoint is needed to resolve VPC names from on premises, and an outbound endpoint and a per-domain forwarding rule are needed to resolve on-premises domains from the VPC, and the IP addresses of both endpoints must be reachable over Direct Connect or VPN. If you specify only the on-premises DNS in the DHCP options, Route 53 Resolver is bypassed and the private hosted zone cannot be resolved. Publishing private records in a public zone exposes internal names. BIND instances are servers that you must operate yourself.

prompt: A global retail company deploys template updates with StackSets to 120 accounts and 3 Regions (ap-northeast-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). The company wants to detect problems quickly and have the operation stop automatically before a faulty template spreads to all Regions and accounts. If failures in the first Region exceed the limit, the operation must not proceed to the remaining Regions. The responsible team cannot watch continuously during the deployment. Each stack instance contains only one or two resources per account, so the deployment itself finishes in a few minutes, and safety takes priority over deployment time. What is the MOST appropriate configuration that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set Region concurrency to Parallel and raise the maximum concurrent accounts to the full count to reduce deployment time, and investigate failures after the operation finishes. If needed, select only the failed accounts and redeploy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set Region concurrency to Sequential and specify the Region deployment order, and set the failure tolerance low, such as 2 stacks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the failure tolerance to 100% to deploy to all accounts for now, and collect only the failed stack instances to retry later.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a separate StackSet for each Region, and have an engineer check each Region's results and then manually start the operation for the next Region.

explanation: The correct answer is to deploy Regions sequentially with a low failure tolerance. When the number of failed stacks in a Region exceeds the tolerance, that Region's operation becomes FAILED, the overall operation also becomes FAILED, and the operations for the remaining Regions are canceled. Parallel deployment spreads to all Regions at once, which does not match the requirement to stop quickly, and raising concurrent accounts only enlarges the blast radius. With a tolerance of 100%, the operation never stops no matter how many failures occur. Chaining separate per-Region StackSets manually replaces the requirement to stop automatically with human work and only adds operational overhead.

prompt: A logistics company wants to continuously scan 200 EC2 instances for software package vulnerabilities. Most are SSM managed nodes, but 15 legacy instances on which regulations prohibit installing an agent (EBS-backed, xfs file system, 3 volumes totaling 600 GB) must also be included in the scan, and the company does not want to make any changes to those instances. The security team wants to see the scan results in one place and cannot operate a separate scanner server. It would be good if the results could be sent to Security Hub CSPM, and all the instances to be scanned are in the same Region. What is the MOST appropriate setting that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fix the Amazon Inspector EC2 scan mode to agent-based and exclude the legacy instances on which an agent cannot be installed from scanning. Compile the scan results into a separate report by hand and share it with the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Amazon Inspector EC2 scan mode to hybrid so that SSM managed nodes are scanned agent-based and the other instances are scanned agentless based on EBS snapshots.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install the SSM Agent as an exception only on the legacy instances to register them as managed nodes, and then scan them agent-based.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty EC2 Runtime Monitoring so that package vulnerabilities on the legacy instances are also detected.

explanation: The hybrid scan mode uses both agent-based and agentless scanning: SSM managed nodes are scanned with the agent, and unmanaged EBS-backed instances are scanned by collecting the software inventory from snapshots. The legacy instances are EBS-backed, use ext4 or xfs, and meet the agentless conditions of fewer than 8 volumes and a total of 1,200 GB or less. The agent-based-only mode scans only SSM managed nodes, so it would miss the 15 legacy instances. Installing an agent violates the regulation that an agent cannot be installed. GuardDuty is a threat detection service and is not intended for package vulnerability scanning.

prompt: In an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB at a video education company, every time a scale-in event occurs, some users are disconnected during report downloads that take up to 90 seconds and receive 5xx responses. The deregistration delay of the target group is currently 30 seconds. Downloads are synchronous requests handled inside the instance, scale-in is performed by a CPU target tracking policy, and scale-in itself cannot be prevented because of cost. Instances must not receive new requests before they are terminated, and the company wants to remove instances as quickly as possible during scale-in to save cost. What is the MOST appropriate adjustment to protect in-flight requests?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the deregistration delay to 0 seconds so that new requests go to other instances as soon as a target is removed, reducing request disconnections.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn off cross-zone load balancing so that only the instances in each AZ handle requests for that AZ, limiting the scope of impact during scale-in.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the target group health check interval to delay the point at which an instance that is scaling in is judged unhealthy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the deregistration delay to 120 seconds, which is longer than the maximum request processing time, so that in-flight requests finish before the instance is terminated.

explanation: The correct answer is to increase the deregistration delay beyond the longest request time. When a target is deregistered, the load balancer stops sending it new requests and, in the draining state, waits for in-flight requests to finish for the length of the delay, and according to the documentation, Auto Scaling also waits for that time or for requests to complete before it terminates the instance. The current 30 seconds is shorter than the 90-second download, which causes the disconnections. Setting the delay to 0 seconds does not protect in-flight requests. The cross-zone setting changes only the scope of request distribution and has nothing to do with protection at termination time. The health check interval does not increase the draining wait time.

prompt: An application at an online insurance company stores the credentials of an application account for Amazon RDS for MySQL in AWS Secrets Manager. Under security policy, the database password must be changed every 30 days, and the application code must not need to be redeployed when the password changes. The application retrieves the secret at startup and when a connection fails. The development team has 5 members and has no capacity to build and maintain a rotation script. The secret contains the user name and password as JSON, and the database is in a private subnet in the same VPC. Which method meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Store the password in a Parameter Store SecureString and run a custom-written rotation script every 30 days on an EventBridge schedule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure automatic rotation on the secret with a 30-day schedule, and have the application read the latest value with GetSecretValue when needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on automatic key rotation for a KMS customer managed key so that the database password also changes every 30 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the password in a Lambda environment variable and redeploy with a new value through the CI/CD pipeline every 30 days.

explanation: Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation on a schedule you specify and updates the credentials in both the secret and the database, and if the application retrieves the secret at run time, it uses the new value without redeploying code. Parameter Store with a custom script requires you to implement and operate the rotation procedure and the database update yourself, so the burden is large. KMS key rotation changes the encryption key material and does not change the database password. Storing the password in an environment variable and redeploying violates the constraint that code must not be redeployed and exposes the password in configuration.

prompt: The operations team at a telecommunications company patches 300 Amazon Linux servers. The policy is to auto-approve, 7 days after release, only patches whose classification is Security and whose severity is Critical. One specific patch that caused an outage in the past must not be installed on any server. The predefined baselines provided by AWS cannot be modified and have approval conditions that differ from this policy. All the servers are managed by Systems Manager, and patching must run automatically on a schedule. Baselines can be created separately for each operating system, and new patches must not be installed right after release but only after 7 days have passed. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set classification and severity conditions and a 7-day auto-approval delay in a custom patch baseline, and add the problem patch to the rejected patches list.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the predefined patch baseline as is, and exclude the problem patch manually in the package manager by connecting to the servers. After installation, compare the package list of each server to check that the exclusion was honored.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Install Override list that enumerates every patch ID to approve by hand, and install based on this list instead of conditional rules.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run only Scan operations periodically to get a missing-patch report, and have an engineer manually install patches on each server after looking at the report.

explanation: A custom patch baseline lets you define the approval targets by classification and severity, supports auto-approval rules that wait a number of days after release, and lets you exclude a specific patch with the rejected list, so it meets all three requirements. The predefined baselines cannot be modified and also approve Important severity and Bugfix patches, so they do not fit this policy, and excluding manually on each server creates consistency and operational overhead problems at 300 servers. An Install Override list uses a fixed list in place of rules, so it cannot express the auto-approval rules and requires you to maintain the list every time a patch is released. Running Scan only reports and installs no patches.

prompt: A financial holding company wants to prevent anyone from stopping or deleting CloudTrail trails in the 40 accounts in a workloads OU in AWS Organizations. The restriction must also apply to each account's administrator roles and root user, and account administrators must not be able to lift the policy themselves. Account administrators already have broad IAM permissions, and the security team has no staff to check settings in each account. The actions to block are StopLogging, DeleteTrail, and UpdateTrail, and the security team's account does not need an exception to this restriction. What is the MOST appropriate method that meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the same deny statement as an inline policy to all IAM roles and users in each account to block CloudTrail changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set a permissions boundary on all IAM users and roles that excludes the permissions to change CloudTrail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Detect that a trail has been turned off with an AWS Config rule and send a notification, and operate so that an engineer turns the trail back on immediately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach to the workloads OU an SCP that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and similar actions.

explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions available to IAM users and roles in member accounts, including the root user, and it can be changed only from the organization management side, so account administrators cannot lift it. Inline policies added to each account can be modified or deleted by account administrators and do not apply to the root user. A permissions boundary applies only to IAM users and roles, so it cannot block the root user, and administrators can also change the boundary. A Config rule only detects after the fact and cannot prevent the stop itself, so it does not meet the requirement to prevent it.

prompt: A database on a 200 GiB gp2 volume at a data analytics company uses little I/O during normal times, but when the daily batch starts, it requires about 3,000 IOPS for more than an hour. When the batch runs long, response times become sharply slower and recover only after a long while. The company wants to confirm the cause and fix it with the least operational burden, without detaching the volume or interrupting the service. The database is OLTP in nature with a lot of random I/O. The current instance is an EBS-optimized type, and increasing the volume size is not preferred from a cost perspective. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Check the CloudWatch BurstBalance metric to see whether the gp2 I/O credits are being exhausted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop the instance, create a new io2 volume from a snapshot and replace the volume, and then start the instance again. Switch the service to maintenance mode while it is being replaced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the volume size so that I/O credits accumulate faster and the burst time during the batch period increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the volume type to gp3 with Elastic Volumes and provision the IOPS needed for the batch.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the volume to st1 to increase sequential throughput and have it handle the database's random I/O as well.

explanation: The correct answers are checking the BurstBalance metric to confirm credit exhaustion and changing to gp3 with Elastic Volumes. The baseline performance of a 200 GiB gp2 volume is 600 IOPS, and when it bursts to 3,000 IOPS the credits run out within a few tens of minutes, so performance drops in a batch that lasts more than an hour, and BurstBalance shows the remaining credit balance. gp3 consistently provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline without bursting and lets you provision more if needed, and Elastic Volumes makes the change without interrupting the instance. st1 does not suit a database with a lot of random I/O. Stopping the instance and replacing the volume with io2 interrupts the service and violates the constraint. Reducing the size would actually reduce credit accrual and baseline IOPS.

prompt: A retail company has a Site-to-Site VPN connecting its headquarters to a VPC, but only one tunnel is configured on the on-premises firewall. Each time AWS performs maintenance on a tunnel endpoint, the connection drops for several minutes and affects the business. The customer gateway device is a model that supports configuring a second tunnel, and BGP is already in use. Introducing Direct Connect is not possible under the current budget. The customer gateway device supports dual-tunnel failover, and the company's network team is comfortable with routing changes. How can the company reduce such interruptions with the LEAST change, without creating a new VPN connection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the tunnel options, extend the Phase 1 lifetime to the maximum so that tunnel renegotiation does not occur and the session stays up during maintenance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the on-premises firewall with a model that has greater processing capacity to improve throughput so that the connection does not drop during maintenance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Also configure the second tunnel provided by the VPN connection on the customer gateway device so that both tunnels can be used.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch to an accelerated Site-to-Site VPN so that the tunnel termination point moves to the AWS edge and the effect of VPC-side maintenance disappears.

explanation: The correct answer is to configure the second tunnel on the customer gateway device. According to the documentation, a Site-to-Site VPN connection provides two tunnels, each with its own public IP address, and when one tunnel goes down for maintenance, traffic automatically switches to the other configured tunnel; AWS recommends configuring both tunnels for redundancy. Changing the Phase 1 lifetime only changes the renegotiation interval and does not prevent a tunnel from going down because of AWS-side maintenance. Increasing firewall capacity does not change the interruption as long as there is only one tunnel. Accelerated VPN is a performance improvement feature and does not address the lack of redundancy of a single tunnel.

prompt: A fintech service must accept connections from a partner using a small number of fixed IP addresses that can be registered in the partner's firewall allow list. The service uses a TCP-based protocol rather than HTTP and runs behind Network Load Balancers in the Seoul and Frankfurt Regions. If one Region fails, traffic must fail over to the other Region immediately, without waiting for the clients' DNS caches to expire. Most clients are mobile apps that often cache DNS responses for a long time, and the partner takes several days to change its allow list. The mobile apps use a DNS cache of up to a few minutes, the service port is a single TCP port, and preserving the client IP address is not required. What is the MOST suitable configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register the NLBs in both Regions as endpoints of an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator, and give the partner the accelerator's static anycast IP addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the TTL of the Route 53 failover records to 5 seconds, and instruct the partner to register the NLBs' current IP addresses in the allow list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register the NLBs in both Regions as an origin group behind a CloudFront distribution, have the partner register the CloudFront edge IP ranges in the allow list, and fail over to the other origin when an origin fails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign Elastic IP addresses to the NLB in each Region and respond with the two addresses by using Route 53 latency records, and have the partner allow both addresses.

explanation: The correct answer is a Global Accelerator standard accelerator. This service provides static anycast IP addresses associated with the accelerator and reacts immediately to health changes by sending traffic to healthy endpoints, and the whitepaper also explains that it avoids DNS caching issues, so it meets both the fixed IP and immediate failover requirements. With DNS methods, even a low TTL cannot prevent some resolvers from caching responses, and the allow list is tied to changes in the NLB addresses. CloudFront is for HTTP and HTTPS content delivery, so it does not fit a TCP-based service, allowing the edge IP ranges is a broad scope, and origin failover works on a per-request basis. Responding with Elastic IP addresses through DNS has the same limitation of waiting for cache expiry.
